history.summary: UNVERIFIED IDENTITY: no web source confirms a distinct, documented Shiv Mandir at Maitri Bagh. Maitri Bagh (Maroda sector, Bhilai, Durg district) is the 111-acre zoo and park established 1972 by Bhilai Steel Plant to mark India-Soviet friendship; travel write-ups describe gardens, zoo, lakes and a musical fountain but no Shiva temple by this name. The well-known old Shiva temple of the area is the Kalchuri-era Deobaloda temple, a separate ASI-protected monument — not to be confused with this entry. The listed Mahashivaratri festival is generic for a Shiva shrine (verify). Coordinates below are for Maitri Bagh park itself and are approximate.

name: Maitri Bagh Shiv Mandir
town_description: Bhilai is the industrial city of Durg district, Chhattisgarh, and the second-largest urban area in the state after Raipur, forming the Durg-Bhilai urban agglomeration with Durg city. It grew around the Bhilai Steel Plant, founded 1955-1959 with Soviet collaboration, and is also an education hub. Maitri Bagh (Garden of Friendship), established in 1972 by the steel plant in Maroda sector, is its best-known public park and zoo, spread over about 111 acres with lakes, gardens and a musical fountain.

travel.airport: Swami Vivekananda Airport, Raipur, about 35-40 km (verify)
travel.railway: Bhilai Nagar / Durg Junction, about 5-10 km (verify)
travel.road: Maitri Bagh is in Maroda sector, Bhilai, on the Durg-Bhilai road network; reachable by city bus, auto and taxi (verify)

visitor_information.opening_hours: Maitri Bagh park is typically open Tuesday-Sunday 9:00 AM-8:00 PM (closed Mondays); temple hours, if any, unverified (verify)
